\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{منگنی} (mangnī)}{منگنی (mangnī)}]{\ur{منگنی} (mangnī) — an engagement to marry}

\label{lesson:UR-C487-mangni}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to pass (of time), then the Urdu for the prime of life.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{منگنی}}
\textbf{\ur{منگنی}} — \emph{mangnī} — \textquotedblleft{}an engagement to marry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میرے} \ur{بھائی} \ur{کی} \ur{منگنی} \ur{ہو} \ur{گئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mere bhāī kī mangnī ho gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother has got engaged.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{منگنی}} (\emph{mangnī}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{maṅgnī}, \textquotedblleft{}betrothal\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{mārgaṇa}, \textquotedblleft{}asking\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10073): the asking for a bride.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mangnī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mangnī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mere bhāī kī mangnī ho gaī.} — My brother has got engaged.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to pass (of time), then the Urdu for the prime of life, then say \emph{mangnī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{منگنی} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An engagement to marry\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\label{lesson:UR-C487-nikah}

Before the new one: say the Urdu for the prime of life, then the Urdu for an engagement to marry.

\ur{مسجد} \ur{میں} \ur{ان} \ur{کا} \ur{نکاح} \ur{ہوا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

Before the new one: say the Urdu for an engagement to marry, then the Urdu for the marriage contract.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سہرا} (sehrā)}{سہرا (sehrā)}]{\ur{سہرا} (sehrā) — a bridegroom's veil of flowers}

\label{lesson:UR-C487-sehra}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for the marriage contract, then the Urdu for the wedding procession.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سہرا}}
\textbf{\ur{سہرا}} — \emph{sehrā} — \textquotedblleft{}a bridegroom's veil of flowers\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دولہا} \ur{کے} \ur{سر} \ur{پر} \ur{پھولوں} \ur{کا} \ur{سہرا} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dūlhā ke sar par phūloṅ kā sehrā thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The bridegroom wore a veil of flowers on his head.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سہرا}} (\emph{sehrā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{sehrā}, \textquotedblleft{}a garland worn at a wedding\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{śēkhara}, \textquotedblleft{}the top of the head, a chaplet\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12604).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{رخصت} \ur{کرنا} (rukhsat karnā)}{رخصت کرنا (rukhsat karnā)}]{\ur{رخصت} \ur{کرنا} (rukhsat karnā) — to see off; to send off (a bride)}

\label{lesson:UR-C487-rukhsat-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for the wedding procession, then the Urdu for a bridegroom's veil of flowers.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{رخصت} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{رخصت} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{rukhsat karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to see off; to send off (a bride)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{رات} \ur{کو} \ur{سب} \ur{نے} \ur{دلہن} \ur{کو} \ur{رخصت} \ur{کیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rāt ko sab ne dulhan ko rukhsat kiyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At night everyone saw the bride off.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{مہمانوں} \ur{کو} \ur{رخصت} \ur{کیا}, \emph{us ne mehmānoṅ ko rukhsat kiyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{رخصت} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{rukhsat karnā}) is built from \textbf{\ur{رخصت}}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{rukhṣa}, \textquotedblleft{}leave, permission\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}: to give someone leave to go.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rukhsat karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rāt ko sab ne dulhan ko rukhsat kiyā.} — At night everyone saw the bride off.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for the wedding procession, then the Urdu for a bridegroom's veil of flowers, then say \emph{rukhsat karnā} again
\end{itemize}
